extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computational algebra system (mathematicians, researchers, and programmers performing linear algebra and matrix-algebra computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation and operational guidance for Magma functions related to vector spaces, linear transformations, row/column operations, solving linear systems, basis changes, field changes, and matrix algebras. Covers semantics, constructors, and examples of usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of a is returned by the function Image(a). It is equal to the product of the whole domain by a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: I := Image(a); I equals V * a. Use to obtain subspace of codomain comprised of outputs of the linear transformation. Distinguish Image(a) from RowSpace(a) which ignores the domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: RowSpace(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: RowSpace(a) returns the space generated by the rows of a, disregarding the domain of a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RowSpace may be of higher dimension than Image(a). Use RowSpace to inspect the span of matrix rows regardless of mapping domain. Example shows RowSpace(a) dimension 2 while Image(a) dimension 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank(a) returns the rank of matrix a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank corresponds to the dimension of the row space (or image when appropriate). Use Rank to verify rank computations indicated by RowSpace dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel(a) / NullSpace(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kernel(a) (or NullSpace(a)) returns the subspace of the domain which is mapped to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ker := Kernel(a); Ker has basis vectors mapping to zero. Kernel is used by Solution and by consistency checks. Multiplying Kernel(a) by a yields the trivial subspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cokernel(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cokernel(a) returns the subspace of the codomain which is not in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cokernel dimension + Image(a) dimension equals dimension of codomain; example shows explicit bases for cokernel generators. Use to inspect parts of codomain not hit by the mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: EchelonForm(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: EchelonForm(a) returns the (row) echelon form e and a matrix b (product of elementary matrices) such that b*a = e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EchelonForm is useful for solving linear systems and for computing bases. Example: e,b := EchelonForm(a) then verify b*a eq e. In matrix-algebra context a,b := EchelonForm(m1) then IsOne(b*m1) can be checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transpose(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose(a) returns the matrix whose columns are the rows of a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown. Useful for converting between row and column perspectives and for constructing Hermitian parts (with complex conjugation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition via multiplication (a*b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplying matrices from different homomorphism modules corresponds to composition of mappings; a*b represents the mapping in Hom(domain(a), codomain(b)) that is composition of a and b when compatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b ∈ Hom(W,U) and a ∈ Hom(V,W) then a*b represents mapping V→U by composition. Use matrix multiplication to represent composition of linear transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary row/column operations (AddRow, AddColumn, MultiplyRow, MultiplyColumn, SwapRows, SwapColumns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to perform the three elementary row and column operations on matrices; each procedure destructively modifies the given matrix, so a tilde (~) must precede its identifier in the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics: AddRow(~a,u,i,j) adds u times row i to row j; AddColumn(~a,u,i,j) adds u times column i to column j; MultiplyRow(~a,u,i) multiplies row i by u; SwapRows(~a,i,j) and SwapColumns(~a,i,j) interchange rows/columns. Example shows creating a copy a1 := a then AddRow(~a1,17,1,4) and SwapColumns(~a1,2,5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution(X, W)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solution(X, W) returns a particular solution v to V*X = W and also returns the kernel K of X (viewing X as a homomorphism). The general solution is v + k for k ∈ K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example solving linear system: v, K := Solution(X, W); verify v*X eq W and Kernel(X) eq K. Use when a solution exists; use IsConsistent to test existence first.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsConsistent(X, W)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsConsistent(X, W) returns true if the linear system V*X = W has a solution; if so it also returns a particular solution and the kernel (as Solution does).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsConsistent when unsure if a solution exists; it returns (false) if inconsistent, or (true, v, K) when consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: VectorSpaceWithBasis(B) and Coordinates(V, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: VectorSpaceWithBasis(B) defines a vector space with chosen basis B. Coordinates(V, v) returns the coordinates of v relative to V's current basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may coerce vectors into either the standard space or the custom-basis space interchangeably for element equality; the basis matters for Coordinates. Example shows Sw := VectorSpaceWithBasis([ ... ]) and Coordinates(Sw, v) giving coefficients relative to that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulating non-standard basis via mapping matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: To simulate a vector space whose entries are radically connected with a non-standard basis, create a matrix m whose rows are the non-standard basis vectors and use its inverse to change coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: m := M![rows]; mInv := m^-1; then S!v * mInv gives coordinates of v relative to the simulated basis. Use EndomorphismAlgebra(S) to obtain the appropriate algebra for m.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIndependent(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsIndependent(S) returns true if the elements of the set or sequence S are linearly independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when incrementally building a basis. Example: vecseq := [...] ; print IsIndependent(vecseq);

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtendBasis(Q, V) / ExtendBasis(U, V)
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtendBasis(Q, V) constructs a basis of V such that the linearly independent sequence Q is the first part of the resulting basis sequence. ExtendBasis(U, V) uses a subspace U and begins the basis sequence with the basis of U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works even when V is not a full vector space. Example demonstrates ExtendBasis(vecseq, V5).

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtendField(V, L)
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtendField(V, L) changes the coefficient field K of vector space V to an extension field L (L must be an extension of K); returns U = V ⊗_K L and the inclusion homomorphism V → U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to work over a larger finite field. Both returned values (space and homomorphism) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictField(V, L)
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictField(V, L) changes the coefficient field of V to a subfield L (L must be a subfield where generating vectors for K lie over L); returns U (V with scalars restricted to L) and the restriction homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when coercing a vector space to a smaller base field; requires the generating vectors for K to lie over L.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChangeRing(V, R[, f])
rubrics_metrics.description: ChangeRing(V, R) coerces the components of elements of V into R, returning the vector space V_R and the homomorphism from V to V_R. If a special homomorphism f from the old coefficient ring to R is needed, use ChangeRing(V, R, f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More general field/ ring change mechanism than ExtendField/RestrictField; returns both new space and mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: MatrixAlgebra(R, n) / MatrixRing(R, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: MatrixAlgebra(R, n) constructs the R-algebra Mn(R) of all n × n matrices over ring R. MatrixRing is an alternative name. Category of such algebras is AlgMat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: M := MatrixAlgebra(F,3) constructs full matrix algebra degree 3 over GF(5). Use when requiring the generic (complete) matrix algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing matrices by coercion (row-major sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: An element of a matrix algebra is constructed by forming a sequence of its entries in row-major order and coercing it into the algebra (M![...]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients in the sequence are coerced into the coefficient ring automatically when possible. Example: m1 := M![2,3,0,1,1,0,0,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: ScalarMatrix, Zero(M), DiagonalMatrix, MatrixUnit
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenience constructors: M!t or ScalarMatrix(M,t) creates scalar matrix with t on diagonal; Zero(M) returns zero matrix; DiagonalMatrix(M,Q) constructs diagonal matrix with Q down diagonal; MatrixUnit(M,i,j) constructs matrix unit with 1 at (i,j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These helpers simplify common constructions and avoid creating full sequences when creating scalar/diagonal/unit matrices. Example usages shown in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eltseq / ElementToSequence(m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eltseq(m) converts matrix m into the sequence of its entries in row-major order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for extracting entries for other constructions or randomness seeding. Example prints Eltseq(m1) = [2,3,0,1,1,0,0,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic on matrices and IsUnit(m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices support usual ring operators for addition, multiplication, and inversion (inverse via raising to power -1). IsUnit(m) tests whether matrix m has an inverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember matrix multiplication is not commutative in general. Example shows m1 * m2 and m1^-1. Use IsUnit before attempting inverse in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic coercion of scalars into scalar matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic coercion allows reference to scalar matrices by the scalar alone when involved in arithmetic with matrices (the scalar is coerced to the scalar matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: m1 - 2 subtracts scalar 2 as scalar matrix from m1; this is forced coercion convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and modifying entries and rows (m[i,j], m[i])
rubrics_metrics.description: m[i,j] accesses or assigns the (i,j)-entry of matrix m; m[i] accesses or assigns the i-th row (as a vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: r := m1[3]; m2[3,2] := 2; m2[1] := r. Use to read/alter specific rows or entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility rules for matrix multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplication of matrices is allowed when coefficient rings are compatible and the number of columns of the first equals the number of rows of the second. This includes rectangular matrices belonging to matrix spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 27 for rectangular matrices and examples. Block operations within matrices are also available (Table 27.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing subalgebras (sub< M | gens > and MatrixAlgebra< R,n | gens >)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subalgebras may be built by first creating generic Mn(R) then using sub< M | generators >, or by constructing the subalgebra directly with MatrixAlgebra< R, n | generator specification > where generators are given to the right of '|'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators of the algebra are exactly those given; the identity of the generic algebra is not automatically included among generators. Example: Ms := MatrixAlgebra< F, 3 | m1 > and Ms eq sub< M | m1 >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a matrix algebra S, Generic(S) returns the generic algebra Mn(R) in which S is naturally embedded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to recover the full matrix algebra corresponding to a subalgebra S. Example: Generic(Ms) eq M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideals: lideal, rideal, ideal and ideal-related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because matrix algebras are generally non-commutative there are left ideals, right ideals and two-sided ideals. Constructors are lideal, rideal and ideal. Functions relating to ideals include JacobsonRadical(M), MaximalIdeals(M), MaximalLeftIdeals(M), MaximalRightIdeals(M), MinimalIdeals(M), MinimalLeftIdeals(M), MinimalRightIdeals(M), IsSimple(M), IsSemisimple(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximal/minimal ideals functions return sequences of ideals in non-decreasing size and accept parameter Limit (default ∞) to cap number of ideals computed; second return value indicates whether all ideals were returned. Examples show building LI := lideal< M | M.1 > and testing ideal closure properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient of algebra (quo< A | I >)
rubrics_metrics.description: quo< T | B > returns the quotient algebra Q and a homomorphism f from the original algebra T to Q. The kernel of f is the ideal B used to form the quotient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Q,f := quo< T | B >; Kernel(f) eq B. Use Morphism to compute explicit correspondence between subalgebras and images; the Morphism matrix is square and full rank when isomorphism holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphism between algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphism(U, V) returns the homomorphism matrix between two related algebras/spaces; frequently used to exhibit isomorphisms between quotient images and subalgebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Morphism(Q, f(D)) returns a permutation matrix showing correspondence, used to verify isomorphism between Q and f(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other matrix-algebra constructions (DirectSum, TensorProduct, ExteriorSquare, SymmetricSquare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to construct algebraic combinations: DirectSum(M,N) and TensorProduct(M,N) for algebras, DirectSum(a,b) and TensorProduct(a,b) for elements, ExteriorSquare(a) and SymmetricSquare(a) for exterior and symmetric square elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to build larger/algebraically-related algebras or to compute standard constructions such as exterior and symmetric squares. Example shows DirectSum of matrices and printing result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree(M), Dimension(M), CoefficientRing(M) / BaseRing(M), Generic(M) facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree(M) returns n for n×n algebra M; Dimension(M) returns dimension (base ring must be a field); CoefficientRing(M) or BaseRing(M) returns the base ring R; Generic(M) returns the full matrix algebra Mn(R) in which M embeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to inspect global properties of a matrix algebra. Table 28.3 summarizes these functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element facts: NumberOfRows, NumberOfColumns, Rank, Determinant, Trace, Transpose, Order, FactoredOrder, IsDiagonal, IsScalar, IsSymmetric, IsSimilar
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions for matrix element properties: NumberOfRows(a)/Nrows(a), NumberOfColumns(a)/Ncolumns(a), Rank(a), Determinant(a), Trace(a), Transpose(a), Order(a) (over finite fields), FactoredOrder(a), IsDiagonal(a), IsScalar(a), IsSymmetric(a), IsSimilar(a,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inspect properties and invariants of matrices. IsSimilar returns true if matrices are similar and also returns t such that t*a*t^-1 = b when true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermitian and anti-Hermitian decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: For A over C, HermitianPart(A) constructs the Hermitian part (transpose plus complex conjugation) and HermAnti returns decomposition A = B + (A - B) where B = 1/2*(A + HermitianPart(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example functions given for constructing HermitianPart and HermAnti; demonstrates that any complex square matrix may be written as sum of Hermitian and anti-Hermitian matrices and shows verification of properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: BaseModule(M) and action on module
rubrics_metrics.description: BaseModule(M) returns the generic R-module (or vector space when R is a field) V of rank n on which M acts. For m in M, the map v ↦ v*m is an endomorphism of V; Kernel(m) and Image(m) return the corresponding submodules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use BaseModule(M) to get the natural module for M. Alternative names: NullSpace(m) and RowSpace(m) for kernel and image in this context. Example: Kernel(m2) and Image(m2) printed with echelonized bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplying submodule by matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: You can multiply a submodule (subspace) and a matrix; e.g., Kernel(m)*m yields image of Kernel(m) under m (often trivial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print Kernel(m2) * m2; yields trivial subspace of dimension 0 in the provided example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eigenspace and canonical-form functions (CharacteristicPolynomial, MinimalPolynomial, Eigenvalues, Eigenspace, JordanForm, RationalForm, InvariantFactors, PrimaryRationalForm, PrimaryInvariantFactors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions for eigen-theory and canonical forms: CharacteristicPolynomial(a), MinimalPolynomial(a), Eigenvalues(a) (set of tuples eigenvalue and multiplicity), Eigenspace(a,e) returns eigenspace for eigenvalue e, JordanForm(a) returns (j,b,block-sequence) with bab^{-1}=j, RationalForm(a) returns rational canonical form f and conjugating matrix b and block polynomials; PrimaryRationalForm and related functions return primary decompositions and invariant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions require the matrix to be square. Use them to compute canonical forms and invariant structures; return values include both canonical form and conjugating matrix plus block structure descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension equalities (rank-nullity and cokernel relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dimension identities: dim(Ker) + dim(Image(a)) = dim(Domain(a)); dim(Cokernel(a)) + dim(Image(a)) = dim(Codomain(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text verify these equalities using Dimension function and print true. Use these to check consistency of computed subspaces.
